extracted.intended_audience: improvisational-theater teachers, actors, students, and comedy performers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for running and assessing improvisational theater exercises (Spolin-style games) to develop presence, specificity, reactivity, and comic material. Includes core principles, purposes of common games, and an explicit five-question performance rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present Moment Awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Games make actors feel grounded in the present. Action and character development arise organically. With scene partners and even the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether performers are focused on the immediate situation rather than pre-planned bits; look for decisions and impulses that arise from current stimuli. (Also appears in explicit rubric: 'Are the players in the present moment?')

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactivity / Spontaneous Response to Partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Players should be reacting to each other (not pre-planned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that offers are accepted and built-on, that performers listen and change direction based on partners' actions; avoid recycled or memorized lines. (Linked to 'Problem-Solving as Theater' — improvisation as responding to in-the-moment problems.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of Where/Who/What
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish setting, character, and activity through specific actions, not exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether performers create concrete specifics (location, relationship, physical actions) through behavior rather than telling. Specific details fuel stronger, more original comedy ('Specificity of "Where/Who/What" → specific comedy').

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from Self-Consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage freedom of expression; discourage self-consciousness; enable fearless exploration onstage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for uninhibited choices, playful risk-taking, and absence of audience-pleasing posture. Teaching/leadership should remove pressure and judgment to permit exploration. (Also: 'Are they free of self-consciousness?' in the explicit rubric.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on the Game (Not 'Acting')
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus attention on the game itself; diminish self-consciousness; unleash creativity so actors 'act' more naturally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether performers attend to the constraints and rules of the game as the driving engine of behavior rather than striving to 'perform' in a theatrical, self-aware way. The game should generate honest behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem-Solving Orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Improvisation = solving problems in the moment; solving them so the by-product is theater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether scenes present and address immediate problems/obstacles that propel action; strong improv treats prompts as problems to be solved rather than setups for jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratization / Nonjudgmental Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes judgment between teacher/student and performers/audience. Choices are never 'right' or 'wrong.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the classroom/ensemble culture encourages participation by removing hierarchical judgment and allowing many choices; this supports risk-taking and exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constraint-driven Comedy (Is the game generating the comedy?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the game (constraint) generating the comedy?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether comedic outcomes arise from the rules and interactions of the exercise rather than from prewritten jokes or performers trying to be funny. The constraint should create opportunities for humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact (game) — physical/verbal alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: For every line you say to someone on stage, you must make physical contact with that person consistent with the intent of the line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this game to evaluate and train physical specificity and congruence between physicality and spoken intent; anti-patterns include touches that contradict spoken meaning or that are perfunctory rather than motivated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mirror (game) — attentiveness and precise imitation
rubrics_metrics.description: One person leads, another mirrors exactly — develops attentiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess performers' ability to observe and match subtle physical detail; the exercise trains listening/seeing skills required for responsive ensemble work. Look for timing, commitment, and shared focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gibberish (game) — nonverbal communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate without language — relies on emotion, intent, physicality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate clarity of emotional intention, physical storytelling, and the ability to convey relationships and objectives without words. Strong gibberish work still feels purposeful and clear to partners/audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status Game — power dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Play scenes at high or low status — reveals power dynamics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use status exercises to assess and develop performers' sensitivity to hierarchical cues and their ability to use status changes as a dramatic/comedic engine. Look for clear status signaling and dynamic shifts.
